name: FL-17
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+10 district with well-funded incumbent Greg Steube seeking another term
Steube holds roughly a 20-to-1 cash advantage over Democrat Matthew Montavon
Prediction markets price Steube's win odds near 95%
No public polling of the race; an independent nominee has raised little money
model.rationale: The Republican-leaning seat, Steube's dominant fundraising position, and markets pricing his win odds near 95% all point to a comfortable hold; Montavon's minimal campaign leaves no evident path to an upset.
model.watch: A large influx of outside spending against Steube or a strongly favorable national environment for Democrats could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Greg Steube seeks another term in this southwest Florida district, which leans about ten points toward the GOP. He enters the general election with roughly $2.1 million on hand after raising $1.3 million, while Democratic nominee Matthew Montavon has raised under $100,000 and holds about $24,000. An independent candidate, Michael Quirk, is also on the ballot but has raised little money.

No public polls cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Steube about a 95% chance of winning. With a well-funded incumbent in a Republican-leaning seat and an underfunded challenger, the race rates as a likely Republican hold, with the main question being the size of Steube's margin rather than the outcome.
